title: Pre-registered gate for the next weekly review: decide GO/PIVOT/KILL on the growth thesis, not another week of knobs
evidence: SOURCE: the weekly review that ran 2026-09-21 09:05 (cron tc-weekly-persona-review, job 8d3ac21799d5) reported 'needs human attention' with two findings and four recommendations, and nothing actioned them -- the 11:25 ops pass closed growth-goal-stalled with 'volume is not the lever' instead. The operating agent OWNS this decision, so it is filed with the criteria LOCKED here rather than re-derived: (1) followers 157 vs the 2.53/day required for 1000 by 2027-08-20 (traj_ratio 0.07); (2) the 10->30 hashtag ramp produced zero engagement lift across five weeks; (3) three pillars (Fashion & Style, Food & Cooking, Lifestyle) carry all of the tiny signal while Beauty/Travel/Fitness/Community sit at 0.0% after 10-14 posts each; (4) reach 1-4 with 0 likes means the synthetic-account distribution is not reaching real people. DECISION (locked now, applied at the 2026-09-28 review): the gate is -- if followers < 170 AND no pillar exceeds 3% average engagement by that review, the thesis gets a GO/PIVOT/KILL decision rather than another tuning pass. Freeze hashtag volume (no further ramps: the ramp is measured to do nothing) and keep the pillar rotation as-is until the gate reads, because the ONE lever that landed today (image-grounded captions, f37136e, verified live on photo 353) has not yet produced a single post it could be judged by -- the 4090 has been held by prx-tg-pixel-posttrain-v3 all day, so renders (and therefore posts) are stalled on a shared resource, not on strategy. Judging the lever before it has run is the same mistake as re-deriving this item every pass.

2026-09-22 11:2xZ ops-triage: GATE READ CORRECTED BEFORE IT FIRES -- the criterion as locked was unreadable at 09-28, because the cohort it reads cannot contain the levers. Three measured facts this pass.

(1) THE METRIC WAS UNBOUNDED, so I fixed the root cause in the repo. WeeklyReview#pillar_stats documented a weekly read (the content-mix task cites "the 7 days ending that date") but posted_posts carried NO time bound: it averaged the persona's LIFETIME posts -- 143 of them, back to 2025-12-16, against 19 in the last 7 days -- and review 6 (09-21 13:00Z) recorded exactly the all-time figures (Fashion & Style 35 posts / 1.952%, Food 9 / 2.222%). The criterion "no pillar exceeds 3% average engagement" was therefore read off a number dominated by nine months of pre-lever posts, and a lifetime mean could only drift DOWN. FIX: REVIEW_WINDOW_DAYS=7 + a window_posts scope, each pillar row now carries window_days=7 so a bare engagement number can never again be misread as weekly. Evidence: spec/services/growth/weekly_review_spec.rb now asserts an out-of-window post cannot move the mean and that an empty window reads empty (9 examples, 0 failures); spec/services/growth/ 103 examples, 0 failures; live read on the production goal after the change -> lifetime posted_posts=143, window_posts=19, per-pillar max engagement 0.000. Companion fix in the same file: a documented dry run (DRY=1 / apply: false) used to WRITE a Growth::Review row AND run evaluate_previous_gates, which reverts content pillars / hashtags on a failed gate -- so "audit only" mutated the persona and left a row the next review reads as prev. Both halves are now gated on apply.

(2) PUBLICATION LAGS THE LEVER BY THE QUEUE DEPTH, so the 09-28 window is ~90% pre-intervention BY CONSTRUCTION. Of the 21 publishable posts (clocks 09-22 17:23Z -> 09-29 10:30Z, dry_out 09-29) only 7 were RENDERED after the content-mix change (applied 2026-09-21T23:35Z, backup ops/backups/content-mix-20260921T233509Z.json) and those publish 09-27..09-29 (posts 347/348/349/350/351/352/353). The 14 publishing before 09-27 were rendered 09-17..09-21 13:00Z, i.e. before every lever. At the 09-28 13:00Z review the published 7-day window will be ~20 posts of which at most 4 post-date the levers, and those will be 1-2 days old with no insights collected yet.

(3) THE PRE-COMMITTED READ, thresholds UNCHANGED (followers < 170 AND no pillar above 3%): the 09-28 review WILL fire the gate -- followers 158 and max pillar engagement 0.000 -- but on a cohort that could not have observed the intervention the verdict is INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE, so it EXTENDS rather than KILLs. Extension rule registered here, BEFORE the read: re-read at the first review whose published window holds >= 5 posts post-dating 2026-09-21T23:35Z that also carry collected insights; measured ETA is the 2026-10-05 review (posts 347-353 publish 09-27..09-29). This is not a threshold change -- it is the condition under which the locked criterion is a valid measurement at all.

(4) WHAT THE VERDICT SHOULD PIVOT ON, from the data already in hand: reach is 2.8/post over the 14d measured set and 3.5/post by month, i.e. each post reaches ~3 people. A post that reaches 3 people cannot be judged on content, so the binding constraint is DISTRIBUTION, not content quality -- and the 7-day-deep queue means every experiment takes ~2 weeks to read. If the post-intervention cohort also reads ~0 reach, the pivot is on distribution/reach (and on queue depth as experiment latency), not on another content lever. That is the question the 09-28/10-05 gate should answer, and it is now answerable on a bounded, self-describing number.

2026-09-22 11:4xZ ops-triage: the fix described in the note above is commit f14c7cd (packs/growth_harness/app/services/growth/weekly_review.rb + spec/services/growth/weekly_review_spec.rb); the why and the verification trail live in that commit message so the next agent reads them without this board. No threshold was changed and no other lever was touched: the queue depth (7 days) is recorded as the POST-gate lever, not moved now, because shortening it mid-gate would change the very cohort the gate reads.
